source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 7.

sections.heading: 1. Heat Transfer
points: **Heat** flows from a **hotter body to a colder** one until both reach the same temperature.
Heat can be transferred in **three ways: conduction, convection and radiation**.

sections.heading: 2. Conduction
points: **Conduction** — transfer of heat through a **solid** by direct contact, from particle to particle, without the material moving.
Example: a metal spoon in hot tea becomes hot at the far end.
**Metals are good conductors**; wood, plastic and air are **poor conductors (insulators)**.

sections.heading: 3. Convection
points: **Convection** — transfer of heat by the **actual movement of a liquid or gas**.
Heated fluid becomes lighter and **rises**; cooler fluid **sinks** → sets up **convection currents** (e.g. boiling water, room heating).
**Sea breeze (day)** and **land breeze (night)** are caused by convection, because **land and water heat/cool at different rates**.
Winds and ocean currents are large-scale convection.

sections.heading: 4. Radiation
points: **Radiation** — transfer of heat as **rays (infrared)**, **without any medium** (can travel through vacuum).
This is how the **Sun's heat reaches the Earth** across empty space.
**Dark, rough surfaces** absorb/emit radiation better; **light, shiny surfaces** reflect it (why we wear light clothes in summer).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Heat flows hot → cold; three modes: conduction, convection, radiation.
Conduction = solids (particle to particle); metals are good conductors.
Convection = movement of liquids/gases (currents); sea/land breeze = convection.
Radiation = heat as rays, no medium needed; Sun's heat reaches Earth by radiation.
Dark surfaces absorb heat; light/shiny surfaces reflect it.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The Sun's heat reaches us by **radiation** (no medium) — not conduction/convection.
**Conduction** needs a **solid**; **convection** needs a **moving fluid** (liquid/gas).
**Sea and land breezes** are examples of **convection**.
**Dark** surfaces absorb more heat; **light** surfaces reflect more.
